facts.text: A thermal camera makes an image from heat emitted by objects and can show a warm person against cold ground in complete darkness.
facts.quote: A thermal camera makes an image from the heat that objects give off, so it can show a warm person against cold ground in complete darkness.

facts.text: Thermal cameras use lenses and detectors built for the long-wave infrared (LWIR) band, roughly 8 to 14 micrometers in wavelength.
facts.quote: long-wave infrared (LWIR), roughly 8 to 14 micrometers in wavelength, far beyond what eyes or ordinary cameras see. A thermal camera's lens and detector are built for that band.

facts.text: Bare metal has low emissivity and can reflect heat from its surroundings rather than show its own temperature in thermal imaging.
facts.quote: bare metal has low emissivity and acts like a mirror, showing the heat of its surroundings rather than its own temperature [Chapter 6].

facts.text: Poor noise equivalent temperature difference (NETD) can cause a thermal camera to fail to distinguish a person from ground of nearly the same temperature on a hot afternoon.
facts.quote: with poor NETD a person blends into ground of nearly the same temperature on a hot afternoon.

facts.text: Simulating a thermal camera requires predicting scene heat radiation using emissivity, temperatures, sunlight loading, wind cooling and often the recent history of the day.
facts.quote: predicting the scene's heat radiation, which needs emissivity, temperatures, sunlight loading, wind cooling and often the recent history of the day

facts.text: Simulating a thermal camera also requires predicting the camera response using spectral band, optics, NETD and processing.
facts.quote: predicting the camera's response, which needs spectral band, optics, NETD and processing [Chapter 6].

facts.text: One 2026 thermal-camera model could be compared with a real camera only qualitatively because the camera's spectral response was unknown.
facts.quote: One 2026 model could be compared with a real camera only qualitatively because the camera's spectral response was unknown

facts.text: The only quantitative validation of the cited 2026 thermal-camera model was indoors.
facts.quote: the only quantitative validation was indoors

facts.text: No validation evidence was found for the cited 2026 thermal-camera model in rain, snow, fog, dust, mud or reflective machinery conditions.
facts.quote: nothing was found for rain, snow, fog, dust, mud or reflective machinery

facts.text: No job-site emissivity dataset exists for thermal-camera simulation, according to the booklet.
The booklet treats the missing thermal-camera validation evidence as an evidence gap, not proof that thermal-camera physics cannot be modeled.
facts.quote: The booklet calls this an evidence gap, not proof that the physics cannot be modeled [Chapter 6].

facts.text: Thermal cameras are attractive for finding people at night, but adding thermal cameras creates a new simulation and validation problem.
facts.quote: Thermal cameras are attractive for finding people at night, but they add a whole new simulation and validation problem

facts.text: Each added sensor type needs its own credibility argument for the collision-mitigation validation program.
facts.quote: each added sensor type needs its own credibility argument [Chapters 2, 6].
